Later, officers arrested Anella 37, and she was charged with the following acts with one count of resisting arrest without violence. While aggravated child charges were initially listed, prosecutors later stated there was not enough evidence to support those counts. According to investigators, the case began after a report of young children running unsupervised in the street, one of them injured. When officers arrived, they found multiple children inside a home described as being an extremely poor condition, with strong odors, little food, and visible injuries on several of the kids. Authorities later confirmed that there had been around 20 prior child protective investigations involving the same household. During the incident, Anella was taken into custody after allegedly resisting officers, including kicking and struggling during the arrest. All seven children involved were removed from the home and placed into protective custody by child services. In court, a judge found probable cause for 15 charges and set her bond at $56,500, despite objections from her attorney.
